schemeTokens.name: --pa-line
schemeTokens.purpose: Rule colour below the stage; follows Material's light/dark scheme.

schemeTokens.name: --pa-muted
schemeTokens.purpose: Muted text below the stage; #b0b0b0 in the dark scheme.

display.purpose: The single page headline on the stage; its middle clause in green.

title-sm.purpose: Sub-headings inside a section: the comparison's two sides, the expectation items.

step-title.purpose: The plain-words name of each demo step, white.

body.purpose: Material prose size; section intros, max 40em.

body-sm.purpose: Setup lines, comparison notes, ruled-list definitions, the authz.why table, proof lines (13.2 to 14.4px).

caption.purpose: The where-it-runs line and the strip caption; Inter fine print in the frame drops to 10.8 to 11.6px.

label.purpose: Mono labels: demo title and status, engine switcher, recording label and pane names, table headers.

code.purpose: Code figures and the protect line; ligatures off. Terminal 11px, recording 11.6px, step statements 10.8px.

shadows.name: dot-halo
shadows.purpose: Ring in the page ground around strip-plot dots so overlaps stay separate. A rule, not elevation.

motion.name: terminal-typing
motion.value: xterm output, as psql prints it
motion.purpose: A clicked step types its statement into its pane; the authored motion of the page.

motion.name: step-lit
motion.purpose: The light moving to the next step, and a step's hover border.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The page's easing, used by the step check.

motion.name: state-settle
motion.purpose: A played step's check fading in.

motion.name: state-quick
motion.purpose: Hover colour and border changes on buttons and the engine switcher.

motion.name: status-pulse
motion.purpose: Status dot while the demo boots.

motion.name: boot-scroll
motion.purpose: Under 960px the hero's boot button brings the demo frame into view; instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transitions and animations stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: 60em: one column; demo frame unpinned under the story; recording panes stacked; terminal screen 480px.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: 40em: steps stack, boot bar wraps, code wraps, tmux panes stack.

components.name: Protect Line
components.description: The one call that protects a table, in the story column, between the engine line and the rules in plain words.
components.html:
The rules live in an authorization engine (here OpenFGA). The documents table points at it with one line:

select authz.protect('documents',
  type => 'document', id => 'id',
  read => 'viewer', write => 'editor');
components.css: .ds-setup { background: #141414; padding: 16px; max-width: 520px; color: #ededed; } .ds-setup p { font: 13.6px/1.55 Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #a3a3a3; margin: 0 0 9px; } .ds-setup p b { color: #ededed; font-weight: 600; } .ds-setup p code { font: 0.92em 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: #d7f5e6; } .ds-setup pre { margin: 0; padding: 12px 15px; background: #0f0f0f; border: 1px solid #2a2a2a; border-radius: 8px; overflow-x: auto; } .ds-setup pre code { font: 12px/1.6 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-ligatures: none; color: #d7f5e6; white-space: pre; }

components.name: File Figure
components.description: Code as a framed file; the key relation in bold green, comments muted. Sequences sit in a list with green numerals.
components.html:
1. Say who is a viewer, once, in the engine's model:

    type document
  relations
    define org: [org]
    define viewer: shared_with or member from org

  2. Point each table at it:

    select authz.protect('documents',
  type => 'document', id => 'id', read => 'viewer');
-- one line per table

components.description: Supporting points as rule-topped items in two columns, never cards.

narrative.overview:
The site is a dark console with the product running inside it. The first thing on the page is a live demo frame (two psql panes, one as anne and one as bob, with three numbered steps under them), and everything around it is set like documentation for that console: plain Inter prose, JetBrains Mono for anything a database or a person types, thin rules between things, and one green that means "on". Nothing is decorated. Depth comes from a ladder of near-black greys and 1px frames, not from shadows or gradients.

The stage (the hero story column and the demo frame) is always dark (#141414 ground, #0f0f0f panes), in both colour schemes, because it is the brand surface and a terminal. The sections below it follow Material's scheme: in the dark scheme they stand on the same ink, in the light scheme they take Material's white with the same green. Below the stage, content is laid out as ruled lists, file-like code figures and plain tables; there are no cards with icons and no feature grid.

The density is that of a well-set README: short sections, generous vertical space between them (72px), and tight, functional spacing inside the console (6 to 12px).
keyCharacteristics: Dark ink stage with a framed terminal beside the story as the hero.
One accent, Supabase green, used for everything that is lit, pressed, done or ready.
Inter for prose, JetBrains Mono for SQL, terminals, pane names and controls inside the console.
Depth by stepped near-blacks and 1px frames; no shadows, no gradients.
Ruled lists, code figures and plain tables below the stage, never icon cards.
Motion is terminal typing and the lit step moving on; everything else is a short state change.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Supabase green is the only accent and the only positive state colour: lit, pressed, done, ready, selected and focused are all green. If something new needs to look "on", it is green; if it does not mean "on", it is grey.

rules.name: The Coral Is Failure Rule
rules.body: The single non-green hue is Failure Coral, and it appears only when something failed. It is never decoration and never a second accent.

rules.name: The Machine Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a person types or a system prints (SQL, terminal output, pane and engine names, file names, scenario names in tooltips, axis labels) is JetBrains Mono with ligatures off. Anything that explains is Inter.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: Display size appears once, on the stage. Section headings stop at 27px.

rules.name: The Frame Not Float Rule
rules.body: A surface is separated by a 1px line and a step on the grey ladder, never by a shadow. If two surfaces need more separation, move one a step on the ladder.

dos: Do keep the stage on Stage Ink (#141414) with Pane Black (#0f0f0f) panes in both colour schemes.
Do use Supabase Green (#3ecf8e) for every lit, pressed, done, ready and focused state, and Deep Moss Ink (#0c2e1e) for anything written on it.
Do separate surfaces with 1px lines (Rule Grey #222 inside the frame, Frame Grey #2a2a2a around it, the 13% scheme rule below the stage) and steps on the grey ladder.
Do set SQL, terminal output, pane names, engine names and table headers in JetBrains Mono with ligatures off.
Do present code as a framed file: a 12px-radius figure with a 1px rule, comments muted and the key relation in bold green.
Do lay out supporting points as ruled lists or a plain table under a 27px headline.

Do limit authored motion to terminal typing and the lit step moving to the next one (a 200ms border and surface change); other state changes are 160 to 300ms colour or opacity transitions, and all of it stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't use gradients or drop shadows for depth.
Don't add a second accent hue; Failure Coral (#f0777b) is for failure only.
Don't put features in a grid of cards or icon tiles; use ruled lists, file figures or a table.
Don't split the hero into a headline over a feature grid; the stage is the story column beside the working demo frame.
Don't lay anything over the demo recording or terminal; controls go in the bar, the steps row, the boot bar or the foot around it.
Don't make scrolling type or run anything; a statement runs only when someone clicks a step or types.
